newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX ends at 6th successive closing high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX ends at 6th successive closing high.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange roared ahead on Wednesday to finish at a sixth successive closing high as fresh capital sought investment opportunities on the Hungarian bourse, market participants said.
"(Investors) feel the need to spend money while having diffculty finding shares which still have room to rise," said Tamas Petheo of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz.
The BUX index soared to a new trading peak of 7,831.80 points before retreating to end at a preliminary 7,813.06 points, up 99.34 points or 1.29 percent.
The BUX index has risen almost 90 percent so far this year and some analysts believe that the trend might reverse.

"On longer-term this market is a little overvalued and may even come down," said Tommy Erdei, analyst at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett in Budapest. "I think there will be a (downward) correction in the next three to six months."
Other analysts also said recently that they believed the Budapest bourse has made most of its gains for the year.
Hungarian shares have benefited recently from money leaving Poland and the Czech Republic for Hungary, and a strong dollar.

Expectations of good first half earnings have also pushed prices higher recently but now most market participants believe that H1 earnings are more or less priced in, therefore major price increases would not be justified after the release of figures.
Budapest bourse listed firms have to submit their first half earnings by August 15.
On Wednesday, recent gainers chemicals TVK and pharmaceuticals Richter set new trading highs of 4,215 forints and 18,995 forints respectively, although both closed below the new peaks.
Elsewhere, trading company Skala-Coop rose almost eight percent to finish at 1,950 forints.
Machinery firm Mezogep closed at a new high of 3,800 forints, up 240, while spirits maker Zwack gained three percent to close at 4,995.
